cards.title: What product
cards.description: Three of Wands: product type, channel, what needs explicit yes
cards.prompt:
Define the release profile. Analysis only — no code, no deploy.

Output:
1. Type: desktop / web / mobile / CLI / library / open source
2. Channel: store, web deploy, GitHub Releases, package manager, other
3. Release criteria
4. What needs explicit yes: publish, signing, production migration, store upload
5. Whether work was Hobby or Production — if known

Type unknown — ask. Do not assume services, payments, containers, or package managers without repo context.
Next: “Does it work”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — profile is clear
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: Does it work
cards.description: Star: only existing tests and builds
cards.prompt:
Find and run only existing builds, tests, and linters in this repository. Do not invent commands.

Show real output. Score 0–10 from facts: 0–6 red, cannot ship; 7–8 shippable with notes; 9–10 clean. No tests — say so; quality unverified. Cannot run for real — do not score above 4. Do not add new tests unless asked.

Below 7 — next is “Fix” in the Production deck. ≥7 — “Any holes”.

The project may be empty — judge only what exists.
Forbidden: inventing facts or holes; inflating score out of pity; giving 9–10 without three facts; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

Always end with this line (N = your 0-10 score):
KEYCODE_SCORE: N
If checks cannot be run, add a second line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA

cards.title: Any holes
cards.description: Ace of Swords: secrets, input, deps — report, not patch
cards.prompt:
Read-only: check security. Do not apply patches. Do not print secret values — only where found.

Check: hardcoded keys and passwords; input validation; known dependency holes if checkable; whether personal data is logged.
Do not invent vulnerabilities. No access to dependency checks — say so.

Output: critical (blocks release) · important · can wait — with evidence for each.
No criticals — “Build the package”.

The project may be empty — no fact = not PASS.
Forbidden: inventing evidence; PASSing out of pity or because “the idea is good”; flattery.
If something critical exists:
KEYCODE_GATE: FAIL
KEYCODE_NEXT: pro-v1/fix
KEYCODE_STATUS: BLOCKED

Otherwise say there are no critical blockers, and:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY

cards.title: Build the package
cards.description: Three of Pentacles: artifact and rollback; publish only after explicit yes
cards.prompt:
Prepare a package or artifact for the profile from “What product”.

Desktop — installer; web — static or image; mobile — app package; CLI — binary; library — package; open source — tag.
Describe build commands, but do not run them without yes. Rollback plan — how to return to the previous version. Installs, DB migrations, signing, store, and production — only after explicit yes. Do not publish. Do not invent commands missing from the repo.
Next: “Instructions”.

The project may be empty — do not invent services or commands.
Forbidden: publishing, signing, deploying, or store upload without explicit yes; inventing missing commands; flattery and claiming “already shipped”.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — artifact or build plan is ready
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: Instructions
cards.description: Hermit: README / notes / install / rollback that matter
cards.prompt:
Update release documentation. Do not spawn extra files. Change files only when asked.

Need what matters: README (what it is, install, run); release notes; how to upgrade; how to roll back. Simple project — short README and notes. Complex — add install and rollback. Library or CLI — examples.
Do not invent commands missing from the repo. No marketing fluff.
Next: “How to watch”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — docs described
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: How to watch
cards.prompt:
Describe the minimum operations after release.

Logs: where to look. Backups: how often, where, how to restore. Failure response — 3 steps. How users report issues. Rollback. Local or desktop product — backups and rollback only; monitoring not required. Open source — how issues and PRs are handled.
External services — only after the user chooses. Do not invent process theater. A simple project needs 3–5 bullets.
Next: “Ready to ship?”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — operations described
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: Ready to ship?
cards.description: Justice: ship only if checks are green
cards.prompt:
Check release readiness. Do not PASS if anything is missing. Do not invent artifacts.

Required: builds and tests green; no critical holes; artifact ready; docs updated; ops plan exists; rollback possible; manual steps known; user confirmed readiness.
Red tests or critical holes — automatic FAIL.
Code problem — “Fix” in Production. Docs — “Instructions”. Build — “Build the package”.

The project may be empty — no fact = not PASS.
Forbidden: inventing evidence; PASSing out of pity or because “the idea is good”; flattery.

End with exactly two lines.
If ready:
KEYCODE_GATE: PASS
KEYCODE_NEXT: release-v1/launch

If not ready (replace fix with quality-audit, security-audit, package, docs, or operations when the problem is there):
KEYCODE_GATE: FAIL
KEYCODE_NEXT: pro-v1/fix

cards.title: Ship it
cards.description: Sun: plan first; publish only after explicit yes
cards.prompt:
Prepare the launch plan. Do not publish, upload, or ship until the user explicitly said to do it.

First: ordered action list; risks; rollback; what needs yes. After confirmation, do only what was confirmed, verify the artifact and availability if possible, record the result.
Do not invent deploy commands. Do not assume services without context.

After launch, recommend the “Idea check” deck, card “Verdict” — based on real feedback, not a new invented idea.

If launch happened, end with:
KEYCODE_NEXT: validate-v1/evidence-review

The project may be empty — do not invent services or commands.
Forbidden: publishing, signing, deploying, or store upload without explicit yes; inventing missing commands; flattery and claiming “already shipped”.

Also end with one status line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — plan ready or launch done
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — need user yes or more data

cards.title: Recap
cards.description: High Priestess: ready / blockers / rollback / next
cards.prompt:
Read this chat. Do not publish anything or change production. Do not invent evidence.

Four short blocks:
1. Ready
2. Blockers
3. Rollback
4. Next step — one card: What product / Does it work / Any holes / Build the package / Instructions / How to watch / Ready to ship? / Ship it

If the release is not ready — say so.
Do not add KEYCODE_SCORE, KEYCODE_GATE, KEYCODE_NEXT, or KEYCODE_STATUS lines.

The project may be empty — write only what is visible in chat.
Forbidden: inventing completed work; writing or changing code; adding KEYCODE_SCORE, KEYCODE_GATE, KEYCODE_NEXT, or KEYCODE_STATUS lines.
